payload.title: Diff UI: side-by-side, navigation, AI summary

payload.note: PARTIAL from this round's work, not a closed ticket. The Compare tab now has the changed/all filter, click-to-focus on a change row, an Export Markdown button, and the change list with per-chapter board counts - that covers i-28de, i-feb7 and part of the display. NOT done: i-fc06 (side-by-side boards with synchronized ply navigation - the tab shows the change LIST, not two boards), i-7046 (progress badges on the rows, though the diff carries the progress overlay), and i-27b4 (an AI summary button; today the assistant sees the compare directory in its context, but there is no one-click summary from the diff). cdp_compare.js passes for what exists.

PARTIAL, and the check is RED on the assertion that matters. Built this round: the board diff carries left_pgn and right_pgn so no second round trip is needed; boards_added/boards_removed are now full BoardDiffs rather than titles (an added chapter's board has a position, and a title cannot show it); clicking a change row fills two boards side by side and a single ply control moves both; a progress badge marks a chapter the reader has finished; filters, focus and Markdown export landed last round. cdp_compare.js still FAILS: the rows it can click have two EMPTY boards, so 'ply 0 of 0' never advances and the side-by-side navigation is not proven. My seed puts the moves on a chapter the diff does not list first, and because every test run adds studies to the same database, selecting by title and by row position both proved unreliable. I am leaving the assertion red rather than deleting it - navigation that has never moved a ply should not be reported as working. Remaining for the ticket: fix the seed so a row with moves is clicked (then i-fc06 is provable), i-7046's badges need a completed chapter in the fixture to assert, and i-27b4 (one-click AI summary) is untouched: the assistant sees the compare directory, but there is no summary button.
The Compare tab renders two Board components from the diff (left_pgn/right_pgn) with one ply control moving both; verified 3 of 3 -> back -> 2 of 3.
A changed/all filter over the chapter rows; the render closure tracks the filter signal (it read get_untracked before, so the list never re-rendered).
Clicking a change row focuses it and fills both boards, jumping to the first divergence ply.
A done badge on a chapter the reader has completed; cdp_compare marks a chapter done and asserts one .progress-badge appears.

An Ask the assistant button writes a question naming both studies into the assistant composer (the draft moved into AppCtx) and switches to its tab; the assistant already carries the compare directory in its context. Verified in cdp_compare: the tab switched and the composer holds the question.

Closed 5/5, and the last two rounds of red were worth it. The Compare tab now has side-by-side boards fed from the diff (left_pgn/right_pgn, so no second round trip), one ply control moving both (measured: ply 3 of 3 -> back -> 2 of 3), the changed/all filter, click-to-focus, a done badge on completed chapters, Markdown export, and an Ask the assistant button that writes a question naming both studies into the composer and switches tabs (the draft moved into AppCtx rather than duplicating an input). THE RED RUNS TAUGHT THREE THINGS: the seed put moves on a chapter the diff did not list first, so the clicked row had two empty boards and 'ply 0 of 0' could never move; the ply buttons used Signal::update inside a closure and did not move until switched to an explicit get_untracked/set; and the assertion clicked FORWARD, which is disabled once a row has jumped to the divergence, so it clicks BACK now. Two of those were the product, one was the test - which is why I would not delete the assertion while it was red.
